chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman, regarding retaliation between her and a man. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, in injuries, until it reaches one-third, it is equal. So when it reaches one-third, the man is higher [in compensation] and the woman is lower.'

key_terms.ارْتَفَعَ: He was raised/higher (referring to increased compensation)
key_terms.الثُّلُث: One-third (referring to the threshold of injury severity)
key_terms.سَفَلَت: She was lowered/lower (referring to decreased compensation)
key_terms.قِصَاص: Retaliation or equal compensation in kind

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in blood money for men and women regarding injuries in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the application of 'qisas' in cases of bodily injury, establishing that compensation is equal for men and women only up to one-third of the full blood money (diyah). Beyond this threshold, the man's liability increases relative to the woman's, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the disparity in full diyah (typically 2:1) begins to manifest once the injury severity exceeds this specific proportion. This ruling highlights the nuanced approach of the Imams in applying gender-based financial distinctions within the broader framework of justice.
